A computer processes information through a complex, synchronized dance of hardware and software components, all orchestrated by the central processing unit (CPU). The processor is the brain of the computer, responsible for executing instructions and performing calculations. It operates by fetching instructions from memory, decoding them to understand what operation is required, and then executing that operation using its internal registers and arithmetic logic units. This cycle, known as the fetch-decode-execute cycle, happens billions of times per second, allowing the computer to handle tasks ranging from simple text editing to complex scientific simulations.
